correctness.rationale: The stationary angular generator closes m_n=E exp(in theta)=r/(r-in omega). Linear generator balances for E X,E Y, E[X exp(i theta)], E[Y exp(i theta)] and E[XY] express J=E[X dY-Y dX]/dt in a rational function of q=r/k,t=omega/k,a=kappa_x/k. Independent symbolic SymPy expansion of these generator moment formulas exactly matched the displayed quartic numerator P and all positive denominator factors, not just numeric cases. P(0)<0, leading coefficient 2a-3>0 for a>3/2, its linear term is negative, and cubic/quadratic signs yield exactly one Descartes sign variation, hence one positive root and strict reversal signs. For a=3/2 all remaining coefficients are negative. Independent x/y Brownian increments have zero cross-quadratic variation and do not enter mixed first moments; J independent of D_x,D_y. Code also derives generator-vs-age integral finite checks; these are corroboration, not proof of all-parameter uniqueness.
residual_risks: Scope excludes angle rotational Brownian diffusion, non-Poisson clocks, oblique heading reset and position reset.

value.rationale: Exact reversal of mean signed orbital area production, despite a fixed-sign angular velocity between resets, is a substantive counterintuitive dynamical phenomenon. The universal uniqueness and sharp stiffness threshold a=3/2 for all angular speeds yield testable mathematical boundaries for angular-reset control; positional diffusion robustness extends model relevance.
residual_risks: Model is an idealized linear trap and perfect principal-axis heading reset, not a validated prediction for all active swimmers.

final_claim: For an active swimmer rotating at constant positive angular speed in an anisotropic harmonic trap, with Poisson resets only of absolute heading to the strong-trap principal axis and no angular diffusion, the stationary Stratonovich orbital current changes sign at exactly one positive reset rate for each stiffness ratio a>3/2 and t>0; at a=3/2 it stays positive at all finite reset rates.
limitations: Result makes no claims for a<=3/2 except the exact equality boundary and high-q sign coefficient.
Positional Brownian noises must be independent; angular noise zero.
